stories.summary: Site navigation, legal pages and error pages

requirements.requirementDescription: The Register page shows Full name, Email address, Password and Confirm password; all are required.
Full name is 2–100 characters after trimming and contains no "<" or ">".
Email address matches name@domain.tld, has no spaces and is at most 254 characters.
Password is at least 8 characters, at most 72 bytes, and has at least one letter and one number; the rule is shown as a hint.
ambiguities: 72 bytes vs 72 characters for non-ASCII passwords.

requirements.requirementDescription: Confirm password must equal Password.
The server re-validates every registration field independently of browser validation.
An already-registered email (any letter case) is rejected with "An account with this email already exists. Try logging in instead."
ambiguities: Conflicts with enumeration protection in AQA-59 AC-4.
assumptions: Assumption (unconfirmed): the product owner accepts revealing that an email is registered, mitigated by rate limiting.

requirements.requirementDescription: Successful registration creates an active account, redirects to Login and shows "Your account has been created and is active. Please log in."
Password fields have a Show/Hide toggle.
Registration attempts are rate-limited per network.
ambiguities: Limit and window are not stated.
AC-10 says "per network" while AQA-59 AC-5 says "per IP".
assumptions: Assumption (unconfirmed): 20 attempts per hour per IP, as currently coded.

requirements.requirementDescription: The Login page has required Email address and Password fields.
Valid credentials log the user in, open the Dashboard and show "Welcome back, <full name>!".
ambiguities: AC-2 says login always opens the Dashboard; AQA-60 AC-2 returns the user to the originally requested page.
assumptions: Assumption (unconfirmed): the Dashboard is the default destination only when no page was requested, as currently coded.

requirements.requirementDescription: Email matching at login ignores letter case.
Wrong password and unknown email both show "Invalid email or password."
Too many failed logins from one IP are blocked for a time window.
ambiguities: Limit and window not stated.
assumptions: Assumption (unconfirmed): 10 failed attempts per 15 minutes, as currently coded.

requirements.requirementDescription: Logout ends the session, returns to Home and shows "You have been logged out."
A logged-in user opening /login or /register is redirected to the Dashboard with "You are already logged in."
While logged in, the header shows name, email, initials and a Log out button instead of Login/Register.
Anonymous visitors to /dashboard are redirected to Login with "Please log in to view that page."
After login the user returns to the page originally requested (same-site paths only).
The Dashboard shows full name, email, status "Active" and member-since date, and never the password or hash.
The session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
A new session ID is issued on login.
State-changing requests without a valid CSRF token are rejected.
A first visit shows a banner with Accept all, Reject non-essential and Customize.
ambiguities: "Equally prominent" is subjective.

requirements.requirementDescription: No optional cookie or optional script before the visitor chooses.
Accept all enables Analytics and Marketing and their cookies are set.
Reject non-essential keeps all optional cookies off.
The preferences dialog shows Strictly necessary always on and disabled, and optional categories unticked by default.
Closing the dialog without saving is not consent; the banner stays.
The choice is stored in cookie_consent for 180 days and the banner does not reappear.
Cookie Settings in the footer lets the visitor change or withdraw consent; withdrawn cookies are deleted immediately.
Each decision is recorded on the server anonymously.
A policy version change invalidates earlier consent and the banner reappears.
The Dashboard shows Analytics and Marketing as Allowed, Refused or Not set.
The header shows navigation for the current auth state and highlights the current page.
ambiguities: "Highlighted" is not defined objectively (e.g. aria-current="page").

questions: AQA-58: Is revealing that an email is already registered acceptable given AQA-59 enumeration protection?
AQA-58: What is the intended registration rate limit?
AQA-58/AQA-59: Should rate limits be stated "per IP address" in both stories?
AQA-59: What are the intended login throttling numbers and the session timeout?
AQA-59: Should AC-2 say the user goes to the originally requested page when there is one (AQA-60 AC-2)?
AQA-62: What is the mobile breakpoint and which CSP directives are required?
AQA-62: How should the current page be highlighted (e.g. aria-current="page")?
